title: Holding chart information constant at 128k with decoded FHIR notes: how does WAHS Engine condensation compare against complete raw FHIR JSON across Gemma 4 (26B, 12B, E4B)?
summary: We ran an information-constant comparison at a fixed 128k (131,072-token) context window where 100% of each patient's FHIR R4 Bundle fitted without truncation in both pathways, with Base64-encoded DocumentReference and DiagnosticReport clinical note attachments decoded to readable UTF-8 text inside the raw FHIR pathway. Across Sofia Alvarez (436/436 FHIR entries included) and Margaret Chen (448/448 entries included) over all 25 WAHS+ scenarios (30 clinical questions Q01-Q15 and 20 privacy and sharing prompts P01-P10; 50 cases x 6 arms = 300 total cells) on an NVIDIA H200 (141 GB HBM3e) via Ollama on UW CIRG cobalt, decoded complete raw FHIR JSON (~55.9k prompt tokens) was compared directly against WAHS Engine's lossless verbatim condensation (~16.2k tokens, 3.46x smaller) across Gemma 4 26B-A4B MoE, 12B, and E4B. All 300 responses were graded blind by GPT-6.2 Sol (Codex CLI, reasoning high) and Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code CLI, reasoning high) using median axis scoring and strict-majority harm consensus.
takeaway: Even when 100% of the chart and all decoded clinical notes fit inside a 128k window, WAHS Engine condensation outperformed complete decoded raw FHIR JSON across every model size while shrinking prompts 3.46x and preserving full source provenance. On Gemma 4 26B, WAHS Engine scored 78.9/100 (74.3 safety-adjusted; 8.48 accuracy, 7.73 completeness, 7.91 relevance; 3 confirmed harms, 0 disputed; 325/325 inline [N] citations resolved; 2.40s median / 3.05s mean latency) versus 71.0/100 for decoded raw FHIR (65.1 safety-adjusted; 8.10 accuracy, 6.26 completeness, 7.46 relevance; 4 confirmed harms, 1 disputed; 1.41s median / 2.86s mean). On Gemma 4 12B, WAHS Engine scored 74.2/100 (70.3 safety-adjusted; 8.04 accuracy, 7.28 completeness; 3 confirmed harms, 3 disputed; 200/200 citations resolved; 3.44s median / 4.35s mean) versus 68.5/100 on decoded raw FHIR (62.8 safety-adjusted; 7.60 accuracy, 6.34 completeness; 5 confirmed harms, 1 disputed; 1.88s median / 4.69s mean). On Gemma 4 E4B, WAHS Engine reached 70.2/100 (65.0 safety-adjusted; 7.85 accuracy, 7.09 completeness; 6 confirmed harms, 2 disputed; 234/234 citations resolved; 1.74s median / 2.20s mean) versus 63.6/100 on decoded raw FHIR (56.2 safety-adjusted; 7.46 accuracy, 5.81 completeness; 6 confirmed harms, 1 disputed; 2 failed abstentions; 1.24s median / 3.00s mean). Decoding Base64 notes at 128k recovered nearly +26 Benchmark points on raw FHIR versus prior 32k truncated runs by restoring clinical note facts such as latex allergy and discharge medication holds, yet raw JSON still trailed by +5.7 to +7.9 Benchmark points and -0.94 to -1.47 completeness points due to structural noise and lack of source indexing. Across all 300 cells, token-budget compliance was 300/300 (100%), inline [N] citation resolution was 759/759 (100% across engine cells), and blinded dual-judge Krippendorff's alpha measured 0.856 harm, 0.807 completeness, 0.792 abstention outcome, 0.778 citation groundedness, 0.708 relevance, and 0.592 accuracy.
